questions.question: Which of the following statements about ions is correct?

options.text: A cation is a negatively charged species.
A group of atoms carrying a net charge is called a polyatomic ion.
Ions are formed only from non-metal atoms.
Sodium chloride consists of neutral sodium and chloride atoms.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A group of atoms carrying a net charge is called a polyatomic ion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **ion** is a charged particle formed by the **loss or gain of electrons** by an atom or a group of atoms. These can be classified into two types: **cations** and **anions**.
 
• A **cation** is a **positively charged** species formed when an atom **loses** one or more electrons. For example, **Sodium (Na+)**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• A **polyatomic ion** consists of a **group of atoms** joined together by covalent bonds, behaving as a single unit that carries a specific **net electrical charge**. Common examples include the **Ammonium ion (NH4+)**, **Hydroxide ion (OH-)**, and **Carbonate ion (CO3 2-)**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Ions are formed from both **metal** and **non-metal** atoms. Usually, **metals** form **cations** (positive ions) by losing electrons, while **non-metals** form **anions** (negative ions) by gaining electrons. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Sodium chloride (NaCl)** is a classic example of an **ionic compound**. It does not consist of neutral atoms; instead, it is composed of **Sodium cations (Na+)** and **Chloride anions (Cl-)** held together by strong **electrostatic forces** of attraction. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is A group of atoms carrying a net charge is called a polyatomic ion.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Formation of Ions:**
 
 
• Atoms participate in ion formation to achieve a stable **noble gas configuration** (octet rule).
 
• The **energy** required to remove an electron from a neutral atom is known as **Ionization Potential**, whereas the energy released when an electron is added is **Electron Affinity**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Polyatomic Ions:**
 
 
• **Oxyanions**: These are polyatomic ions that contain **oxygen**, such as **Sulfate (SO4 2-)**, **Nitrate (NO3-)**, and **Phosphate (PO4 3-)**.
 
• **Monatomic Ions**: Unlike polyatomic ions, these consist of only a **single atom** with a charge, such as **Magnesium ion (Mg2+)** or **Fluoride ion (F-)**.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Formulas of Ionic Compounds:**
 
 
• When writing formulas for compounds containing **polyatomic ions**, the ion is often enclosed in **brackets** if a subscript is needed to indicate its **numerical ratio** (e.g., **Mg(OH)2**).
 
• The total positive charge must **balance** the total negative charge to ensure the compound is **electrically neutral**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Valency:** This refers to the **combining capacity** of an atom or a group of atoms. For ions, the **valency** is equal to the magnitude of the **charge** it carries. For instance, the valency of **Aluminum (Al3+)** is **3**.
 
• **Size Comparison:**
 
 
• A **cation** is always **smaller** than its parent neutral atom because the loss of electrons reduces electron-electron repulsion and often results in the loss of an entire **shell**.
 
• An **anion** is always **larger** than its parent neutral atom due to increased **repulsion** between the extra electrons.
 
 
 
• **Electrolytes:** Substances that dissociate into ions when dissolved in **water** or melted are called **electrolytes**. These ions act as **charge carriers**, allowing the solution to conduct **electricity**.
</ul

questions.question: Through which of the following structures does urine go into the urinary bladder from kidneys?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ureters**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ureters** are narrow, hollow, **muscular tubes** that connect the **kidneys** to the **urinary bladder**. Each person typically has **two ureters**, one attached to each kidney.
 
• The primary function of the **ureter** is to transport **urine**, which is continuously formed by the **kidneys**, down to the **urinary bladder** for storage. ***Hence, the correct answer is Ureters.***
 
• Urine does not simply flow down due to gravity; the walls of the **ureters** contract and relax in **peristaltic waves**. These rhythmic contractions occur about **one to five times per minute** to push urine toward the bladder.
 
• In an adult, the **ureters** are approximately **25 to 30 cm (10 to 12 inches)** long and have a diameter of about **3 to 4 mm**.
 
• The **ureters** enter the **urinary bladder** at an **oblique angle** through the bladder wall. This specific anatomical arrangement acts like a **valve**, preventing the **backflow (reflux)** of urine from the bladder back into the kidneys when the bladder is full or during **micturition** (urination).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vena Cava**:
 
 
• The **Vena Cava** is the **largest vein** in the human body. There are two parts: the **Superior Vena Cava** (carrying blood from the upper body) and the **Inferior Vena Cava** (carrying blood from the lower body).
 
• Its primary function is to transport **deoxygenated blood** from various parts of the body back to the **right atrium** of the **heart**. It is part of the **circulatory system**, not the **urinary system**.
 
 
 
• **Artery**:
 
 
• **Arteries** are blood vessels that carry **oxygenated blood** away from the **heart** to the rest of the body (except for the pulmonary artery).
 
• In the context of the renal system, the **Renal Artery** supplies **oxygen-rich and unfiltered blood** from the **Aorta** to the **kidneys**.
 
 
 
• **Vein**:
 
 
• **Veins** are blood vessels that carry **deoxygenated blood** toward the **heart**.
 
• The **Renal Vein** carries **filtered, deoxygenated blood** away from the **kidneys** to the **Inferior Vena Cava**. Neither arteries nor veins carry urine; they carry blood.
 
 
 
• **Urinary Bladder**:
 
 
• The **Urinary Bladder** is a **muscular, pear-shaped sac** located in the **pelvic cavity**. It serves as a temporary reservoir for **urine**.
 
• The bladder wall contains the **detrusor muscle**, which contracts to expel urine during urination. An average adult bladder can hold between **400 to 600 ml** of urine.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Human Excretory System**:
 
 
• The main components include a **pair of kidneys**, a **pair of ureters**, a **urinary bladder**, and a **urethra**.
 
• The **Kidneys** are the primary organs for **homeostasis**, filtering approximately **120 to 150 quarts of blood** daily to produce about **1 to 2 quarts of urine**.
 
• The **Urethra** is the tube that conveys **urine** from the **urinary bladder** to the **outside of the body**. In males, it also serves as a passage for **semen**, whereas in females, it is strictly part of the **urinary system**.
 
• **Renal Pelvis**: This is the funnel-like dilated proximal part of the **ureter** in the kidney where urine collects before entering the tube.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements best differentiates a mixture from a compound?

options.text: A compound can be separated into its constituents by physical methods.
A compound shows the properties of its constituent elements.
A mixture always contains elements in a fixed ratio.
A mixture retains the individual properties of its constituents.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A mixture retains the individual properties of its constituents**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **mixture** is a substance made by combining two or more different materials in such a way that no **chemical reaction** occurs. Because no new chemical bonds are formed, each constituent substance in a **mixture** keeps its own **physical and chemical properties**. For example, in a mixture of **iron filings** and **sulfur powder**, the iron remains magnetic and the sulfur remains yellow. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• A **compound** is a substance formed when two or more **chemical elements** are **chemically bonded** together. Once bonded, the **constituent elements** lose their original properties and the resulting **compound** has entirely new characteristics. For instance, **Liquid Water** (H2O) is formed from **Hydrogen** and **Oxygen**, which are both gases at room temperature. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Compounds** cannot be separated into their constituents by **physical methods** such as **filtration**, **distillation**, or **decantation**. They require **chemical methods** or **electrochemical reactions** (like **electrolysis**) to break the **chemical bonds**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• A **mixture** does not have a **fixed ratio**; its **composition is variable**. You can mix **salt** and **sand** in any proportion. In contrast, **compounds** always contain elements in a **fixed, definite proportion by mass**, according to the **Law of Definite Proportions**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Mixtures**:
 
 
• **Homogeneous Mixtures**: These have a **uniform composition** throughout. Examples include **Air**, **Alloys** like **Brass**, and **Salt solutions**.
 
• **Heterogeneous Mixtures**: These have a **non-uniform composition** and visible boundaries of separation. Examples include **Oil and Water**, **Soil**, and **Mixture of pulses and stones**.
 
 
 
• **Energy Changes**:
 
 
• During the formation of a **mixture**, **energy** (in the form of **heat**, **light**, or **sound**) is usually neither absorbed nor evolved.
 
• In the formation of a **compound**, **energy** is almost always involved as **chemical bonds** are either broken or created.
 
 
 
• **Melting and Boiling Points**:
 
 
• **Compounds** have **sharp and fixed melting and boiling points** because of their definite structure.
 
• **Mixtures** do not have fixed melting or boiling points; they melt or boil over a **range of temperatures** depending on the concentration of their components.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Law of Constant Proportions**: Proposed by **Joseph Proust** in **1799**, it states that a **chemical compound** always contains exactly the same **proportion of elements by mass**. This is a fundamental differentiator from **mixtures**.
 
• **Constituent Identity**: In **Chemistry**, the "identity" of a substance refers to its **molecular structure**. In a **mixture**, the molecules of **substance A** and **substance B** simply coexist. In a **compound**, **substance A** and **B** react to form a new **molecule C**.
 
• **Separation Techniques**: **Mixtures** are separated using **physical properties** like **solubility**, **density**, **boiling point**, or **magnetism**. For example, **fractional distillation** is used to separate **crude oil** (a mixture) into its components.
</ul

questions.question: A car slows down uniformly when brakes are applied, producing an acceleration of 8 { m/s}² opposite to its motion. If the car comes to rest in 2s, what distance does it cover before stopping?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**16 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The problem states that the car produces an **acceleration** of **8 m/s²** opposite to its motion. In physics, when acceleration is opposite to the direction of velocity, it is termed **retardation** or **deceleration**. Therefore, we take the **numerical value** of acceleration (**a**) as **-8 m/s²**.
 
• Since the car comes to a complete halt, its **final velocity (v)** is **0 m/s**. The **time (t)** taken to stop is given as **2 seconds**.
 
• To find the **distance (s)**, we first need to determine the **initial velocity (u)** using the **first equation of motion**: **v = u + at**. Substituting the values, **0 = u + (-8 × 2)**, which gives **u = 16 m/s**.
 
• Once the **initial velocity** is known, we apply the **second equation of motion**: **s = ut + ½at²** to find the distance. ***Hence, the calculation becomes s = (16 × 2) + ½ × (-8) × (2)²***.
 
• Solving this yields **s = 32 - 16 = 16 meters**. This represents the **total displacement** of the car from the moment the brakes were applied until it reached a standstill. ***Hence, the calculated distance is correct.***
 
• Alternatively, the **third equation of motion** (**v² = u² + 2as**) can be used. Plugging in the values: **0² = 16² + 2 × (-8) × s**, which results in **0 = 256 - 16s**, or **s = 16 m**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 16 m.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kinematic Equations:** These equations describe the **motion of objects** under **constant acceleration**. They relate five variables: **displacement (s)**, **initial velocity (u)**, **final velocity (v)**, **acceleration (a)**, and **time (t)**.
 
• **Uniform Acceleration:** This refers to a scenario where the **velocity** of an object changes by the same **numerical value** in every equal **interval of time**. In this question, the car slows down **uniformly**, meaning the **rate of change of velocity** remains constant at **8 m/s²**.
 
• **Retardation:** Also known as **negative acceleration**, it occurs when the **force** applied (like **braking force**) is in the direction opposite to the **displacement**. It results in a decrease in the **magnitude of velocity** over time.
 
• **SI Units:** In **physics**, it is crucial to use standard **International System of Units**. Here, distance is measured in **meters (m)**, time in **seconds (s)**, velocity in **meters per second (m/s)**, and acceleration in **meters per second squared (m/s²)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sign Convention:** While solving **mechanics** problems, assigning the correct **sign (+ or -)** to vectors is vital. If **motion** is taken as **positive**, then **braking acceleration** must be **negative**.
 
• **Area under V-T Graph:** The **distance covered** can also be calculated by finding the **area under a velocity-time graph**. For a car slowing down from **16 m/s** to **0 m/s** in **2 seconds**, the graph forms a **triangle**. Area = **½ × base × height** = **½ × 2 × 16 = 16 m**.
 
• **Braking Distance:** The distance covered after applying **brakes** is influenced by the **initial speed** and the **braking efficiency** (acceleration). In real-world **automotive engineering**, this is a key **safety metric**.

questions.question:
A body weighs 60 kg wt on the surface of the moon. What will be the mass and the weight, respectively, of the body on the surface of the Earth?

(Take the value of g on Earth as 10 { m/s}² )
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**360 kg and 360 kg wt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The weight of an object is the force with which it is attracted towards the center of a celestial body. The **acceleration due to gravity on the Moon** is approximately **1/6th** of the **acceleration due to gravity on Earth**.
 
• Consequently, the **weight** of any object on the **Moon** is **1/6th** of its **weight on Earth**. The relation can be expressed as: **Weight on Earth = 6 x Weight on Moon**.
 
• In the given problem, the body weighs **60 kg wt** on the **surface of the Moon**. To find its weight on Earth: **Weight on Earth = 6 x 60 kg wt = 360 kg wt**.
 
• **Mass** is a measure of the amount of matter contained in a body. Unlike weight, **mass is a constant quantity** and does not change regardless of the **location** or the **gravitational field** acting upon it.
 
• The unit **kg wt** (kilogram-weight) is a gravitational unit of force. By definition, **1 kg wt** is the force exerted by **Earth's gravity** on a mass of **1 kg**. Therefore, if a body weighs **360 kg wt** on Earth, its **mass** is exactly **360 kg**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mass:**
 
 
• It is the **intrinsic property** of a body that determines its **inertia**.
 
• The **S.I. unit** of mass is the **kilogram (kg)**.
 
• It is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has only magnitude and no direction. It remains the same on **Earth**, the **Moon**, or even in **outer space**.
 
 
 
• **Weight:**
 
 
• It is the **gravitational force** acting on an object. The formula is **W = m x g**, where **m** is mass and **g** is the **acceleration due to gravity**.
 
• The **S.I. unit** of weight is the **Newton (N)**, but it is often expressed in **kg wt** for practical purposes.
 
• It is a **vector quantity** because it always acts vertically downwards towards the center of the planet.
 
 
 
• **Conversion between Units:**
 
 
• On Earth, where **g** is approximately **10 m/s²**, a weight of **360 kg wt** is equivalent to **3600 Newtons** (360 kg x 10 m/s²).
 
• The **Moon's gravity** is approximately **1.62 m/s²**, which is why objects feel much lighter there even though their **mass** remains unchanged.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Constant vs Variable:** **Mass** is an **absolute** and **constant** value for a specific body, whereas **weight** is a **variable** value that depends on the local **acceleration due to gravity (g)**.
 
• **Calculating Mass from kg wt:** When weight is given in **kg wt**, the numerical value of the weight on **Earth** is equal to the numerical value of the **mass in kg**. This is a common point of confusion in physics problems.
 
• **The 1/6th Ratio:** This ratio is derived from the fact that the **Moon** has a smaller mass and radius compared to **Earth**. The actual ratio is roughly **0.165**, but for general calculations and exams, the fraction **1/6** is the standard convention.
 
• If the question asks for **mass on the Moon**, it would still be **360 kg**, as mass never changes with the change in **gravity**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following organelles is the first to divide during binary fission in Amoeba?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nucleus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Binary fission** in **Amoeba** is a method of **asexual reproduction** where a single parent cell divides into two equal daughter cells.
 
• The very first step in this process is the division of the **nucleus**, a biological stage known as **karyokinesis**.
 
• During **karyokinesis**, the **nucleus** of the **Amoeba** begins to elongate and develop a constriction in the middle, eventually splitting the **genetic material** into two separate parts.
 
• Once the **nucleus** has successfully divided into two daughter nuclei, the second stage, called **cytokinesis**, begins. This is the division of the **cytoplasm**.
 
• In **cytokinesis**, the cell body constricts and pinches off, resulting in the formation of two distinct, independent **Amoeba** individuals. ***Hence, the nucleus is the first organelle to divide during this process.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Amoeba:** 
 
 
• It is a **unicellular eukaryote** belonging to the kingdom **Protista**. 
 
• **Amoeba proteus** is one of the most common species studied in biology. It was first discovered in **1755** by **August Johann Rösel von Rosenhof**.
 
• It lacks a **cell wall** and instead possesses a flexible **plasma membrane**, which allows it to change shape and move using **pseudopodia** (false feet).
 
 
 
• **Cytoplasm:**
 
 
• The **cytoplasm** is the jelly-like substance where most metabolic activities occur. During **binary fission**, it only begins its division after the **nucleus** has finished its separation to ensure each daughter cell receives a copy of the **DNA**.
 
 
 
• **Vacuole:**
 
 
• **Amoebae** contain **contractile vacuoles** for **osmoregulation** and **food vacuoles** for digestion. While these may be replicated or distributed during fission, they are not the primary drivers or the first to initiate the division process.
 
 
 
• **Cell Wall:**
 
 
• This option is incorrect because **Amoeba** is an animal-like protist and does not possess a **cell wall**. **Cell walls** are typically found in **plants**, **fungi**, and **bacteria**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Asexual Reproduction:** Since only one parent is involved and the offspring are **genetically identical** to the parent, the daughter cells are often referred to as **clones**.
 
• **Environmental Conditions:** **Binary fission** typically occurs during **favorable conditions** (adequate food and temperature). During unfavorable conditions, **Amoeba** may undergo **multiple fission** or **encystment**.
 
• **Irregular Binary Fission:** In **Amoeba**, **binary fission** is described as **"irregular"** because the plane of cytoplasmic division can occur in any direction, unlike in **Leishmania** (longitudinal) or **Paramecium** (transverse).
 
• **Mitosis:** The nuclear division in **Amoeba** involves a process similar to **mitosis**, where the **chromosomes** are replicated and distributed equally, ensuring the continuity of **biological information** across generations.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why combination reactions are often exothermic?

options.text: They involve formation of bonds, which absorb energy.
They release energy due to stable product formation.
They involve the breaking of bonds only.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They release energy due to stable product formation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **combination reaction** (also known as a **synthesis reaction**) is a reaction where **two or more elements or compounds** combine to form a **single compound**. The general form is **A + B → AB**.
 
• In any chemical reaction, **energy** is required to **break existing bonds** in the reactants (an **endothermic** process), and **energy** is **released** when **new bonds** are formed in the products (an **exothermic** process).
 
• Combination reactions are generally **exothermic** because the **energy released** during the **formation of new bonds** in the product is **greater** than the **energy absorbed** to break the bonds of the reactants. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The formation of a **stable product** means the system moves to a **lower energy state**. This excess **internal energy** is liberated into the **surroundings**, usually in the form of **heat** or **light**.
 
• Statement 1 is incorrect because **bond formation** always **releases energy**, while **bond breaking** absorbs it. Statement 4 is incorrect as combination reactions primarily focus on **bond formation** to create a complex molecule from simpler ones.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Common Examples of Combination Reactions:**
 
 
• **Burning of Coal:** When **carbon (C)** burns in the presence of **oxygen (O2)**, it forms **carbon dioxide (CO2)** and releases a significant amount of heat. (**C + O2 → CO2 + Heat**).
 
• **Formation of Water:** The reaction between **hydrogen gas (H2)** and **oxygen gas (O2)** to form **liquid water (H2O)** is highly **exothermic**.
 
• **Slaking of Lime:** The reaction of **Quick Lime (Calcium Oxide - CaO)** with **water (H2O)** to form **Slaked Lime (Calcium Hydroxide - Ca(OH)2)** produces a large amount of heat, making the container hot.
 
 
 
• **Thermodynamic Perspective:**
 
 
• In an **exothermic reaction**, the change in **enthalpy (ΔH)** is **negative**. This indicates that the **enthalpy of the products** is lower than the **enthalpy of the reactants**.
 
• Most **spontaneous** combination reactions occur because the universe tends toward states of **lower energy** and **higher stability**.
 
 
 
• **Contrast with Decomposition Reactions:**
 
 
• Unlike combination reactions, **decomposition reactions** involve the breaking down of a single compound into two or more simpler substances. These typically require an input of energy (heat, light, or electricity) and are therefore **endothermic**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bond Energy:** The **strength** of the bonds in the product determines how much energy is released. Stronger bonds in the **product** compared to the **reactants** lead to a more **exothermic** reaction.
 
• **Stability:** In chemistry, **lower energy** is synonymous with **higher stability**. Therefore, the drive to form more **stable chemical species** is the primary reason why these reactions release energy.
 
• **Activation Energy:** Even though combination reactions release energy, they may still require a small amount of **initial energy** (activation energy), such as a **spark** or **flame**, to start the process.

questions.question: Carbon has the unique ability to form bonds with other atoms of carbon, giving rise to large molecules. This property is called:
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Catenation** is the unique property of **carbon** atoms to link with one another through **covalent bonds** to form long chains, branched chains, and closed ring structures.
 
• This property is primarily due to the **small size** of the carbon atom and the **high strength** of the **carbon-carbon (C-C) bond**.
 
• The **bond energy** of the C-C bond is approximately **348 kJ/mol**, which is significantly higher than that of other elements like **silicon** or **sulfur**, allowing for stable, long-chain molecules.
 
• Because of catenation, carbon forms the structural backbone of millions of **organic compounds**, including **hydrocarbons**, proteins, and DNA. ***Hence, option 2 is correct.***
 
• The **tetravalency** of carbon (valency of **4**) further supports catenation by allowing each carbon atom to bond with up to four other atoms, facilitating complex **molecular architectures**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Addition Reaction**:
 
 
• In organic chemistry, an **addition** reaction occurs when two or more molecules combine to form a larger one. This typically happens in **unsaturated compounds** like **alkenes** and **alkynes**.
 
• For example, the **hydrogenation** of ethene to ethane is an addition reaction. It does not refer to the property of atoms linking to themselves. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Conjugation**:
 
 
• **Conjugation** refers to the overlap of **p-orbitals** across an adjacent **sigma bond**, typically in a system of alternating single and multiple bonds.
 
• This leads to the **delocalization** of electrons, which increases the stability of the molecule (e.g., in **benzene**). While it involves carbon bonding, it is a specific electronic arrangement rather than the basic property of forming large molecules. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Unification**:
 
 
• **Unification** is not a standard chemical term used to describe the bonding properties or the molecular structural ability of carbon atoms. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Other Elements showing Catenation**:
 
 
• While carbon is the leader in catenation, **Silicon** also shows this property but can only form chains of up to **7 or 8 atoms** because the Si-Si bonds are weaker and more reactive toward oxygen and water.
 
• **Sulfur** shows catenation in the form of **S8 rings** and long chains in plastic sulfur, but it lacks the structural variety found in carbon compounds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Allotropes of Carbon**: The property of catenation is vividly seen in carbon's **allotropes** such as **Diamond** (3D network), **Graphite** (hexagonal layers), and **Fullerenes** (spherical cages like **C60**).
 
• **Isomerism**: Catenation allows for different arrangements of the same number of atoms, leading to **structural isomerism**. For instance, **butane** and **isobutane** have the same formula (**C4H10**) but different linkages.
 
• **Economic and Biological Importance**: The ability of carbon to form stable chains is the reason for the existence of **fossil fuels** (long-chain alkanes) and the complex **biopolymers** that make up living organisms.
 
• **Atomic Number**: Carbon has an **atomic number of 6** and its electronic configuration is **2, 4**, which provides the perfect balance for forming stable **covalent bonds**.

questions.question: ___________ is/are NOT selectively re-absorbed from the filtrate in the nephron.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Urea**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Nephron** is the basic functional and structural unit of the **Kidney**, responsible for filtering the blood and forming urine.
 
• Urine formation involves three main processes: **Glomerular Filtration**, **Selective Reabsorption**, and **Tubular Secretion**.
 
• **Selective Reabsorption** is the process where the renal tubule reclaims useful substances from the **Glomerular Filtrate** back into the bloodstream. This occurs primarily in the **Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT)**.
 
• Substances like **Glucose**, **Amino acids**, and certain **Salts** are highly useful to the body and are almost entirely reabsorbed via active or passive transport. ***Hence, options 1, 2, and 4 are selectively re-absorbed.***
 
• **Urea** is a nitrogenous waste product formed in the **Liver**. The primary function of the kidney is to **excrete urea** from the body. While a small amount may passively diffuse back to maintain medullary osmotic pressure, it is **NOT selectively re-absorbed** for conservation like nutrients. ***Hence, statement 3 is the correct answer.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Glucose Reabsorption**:
 
 
• Under normal physiological conditions, **100%** of the filtered **Glucose** is reabsorbed in the **PCT**.
 
• If blood glucose levels exceed the **Renal Threshold** (approximately **180 mg/dL**), the transport carriers become saturated, and glucose is excreted in the urine, a condition known as **Glycosuria**, often associated with **Diabetes Mellitus**.
 
 
 
• **Amino Acids**:
 
 
• Like glucose, **Amino acids** are vital nutrients. They are completely reabsorbed in the **Proximal Convoluted Tubule** through **Secondary Active Transport** mechanisms.
 
 
 
• **Salts and Electrolytes**:
 
 
• The body reabsorbs **Sodium (Na+)**, **Potassium (K+)**, and **Chloride (Cl-)** to maintain **Electrolyte Balance** and blood pressure.
 
• About **65-70%** of filtered **Sodium** is reabsorbed in the **PCT**, while the **Distal Convoluted Tubule (DCT)** performs conditional reabsorption under the influence of the hormone **Aldosterone**.
 
 
 
• **Urea and Waste Excretion**:
 
 
• **Urea** is produced through the **Ornithine Cycle** in the liver to detoxify ammonia.
 
• The concentration of **Urea** increases as the filtrate moves down the tubule because water is reabsorbed, ensuring that the majority of this waste is eliminated in **Urine**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR)**: This is the volume of filtrate formed by both kidneys per minute, typically about **125 mL/min** in a healthy adult.
 
• **Tubular Secretion**: This is the opposite of reabsorption, where substances like **Hydrogen ions (H+)**, **Potassium (K+)**, and **Ammonia (NH3)** are moved from the blood into the tubule to maintain **Ionic Balance** and **pH** of body fluids.
 
• **Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH)**: Also known as **Vasopressin**, it acts on the **Collecting Ducts** to increase water reabsorption, thereby concentrating the urine and preventing dehydration.
 
• **Henle's Loop**: Plays a critical role in the **Counter-Current Mechanism**, which helps in concentrating the urine by creating an osmotic gradient in the kidney medulla.
</ul

questions.question: If the length of a conductor and area is halved, keeping material same, then its resistance will ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Remain same**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Resistance (R)** of a conductor is a property that opposes the flow of electric current. It is mathematically defined by the formula **R = ρ(L/A)**, where **ρ** represents the **resistivity** of the material, **L** is the **length**, and **A** is the **cross-sectional area**.
 
• In the given scenario, the **length** of the conductor is **halved**, which means the new length is **L/2** or **0.5L**.
 
• Similarly, the **cross-sectional area** is also **halved**, making the new area **A/2** or **0.5A**.
 
• When these new values are substituted into the resistance formula, the expression becomes **R' = ρ × (L/2) / (A/2)**. The **numerical value** of **1/2** in the numerator and **1/2** in the denominator cancel each other out completely.
 
• Since the **material** remains the same, the **resistivity (ρ)** remains constant. As a result, the new resistance **R'** is exactly equal to the original resistance **R**. ***Hence, the statement that the resistance remains the same is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Resistivity (ρ):**
 
 
• It is an intrinsic property of a material that quantifies how strongly it resists electric current. Its **SI unit** is the **Ohm-meter (Ω·m)**.
 
• Unlike **resistance**, **resistivity** does not depend on the **dimensions** (length or area) of the object; it only depends on the **nature of the material** and the **temperature**.
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law:**
 
 
• Discovered by **George Simon Ohm** in **1827**, this law states that the **current (I)** through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the **voltage (V)** across the two points, provided physical conditions like **temperature** remain constant. The constant of proportionality is **Resistance (R)**.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Resistance:**
 
 
• **Length:** Resistance is **directly proportional** to the length of the conductor. Doubling the length doubles the resistance.
 
• **Area:** Resistance is **inversely proportional** to the cross-sectional area. Increasing the thickness of a wire reduces its resistance.
 
• **Nature of Material:** Different materials have different concentrations of free electrons. For example, **Silver** has lower resistance than **Iron**.
 
• **Temperature:** For **metallic conductors**, resistance generally increases with an increase in **temperature**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Distinction between Independent Change and Stretching:** 
 
 
• It is **important** to distinguish between changing dimensions independently and **stretching** a wire. If a wire is **stretched** to double its length, its **volume** remains constant, causing the **area** to decrease. In such cases, the resistance would change by a **factor of 4** (square of the change in length).
 
• However, in this specific question, both **length** and **area** are explicitly and independently **halved**, resulting in no net change to the **resistance**.
 
 
 
• **Conductance and Conductivity:**
 
 
• The reciprocal of **resistance** is known as **conductance (G)**, measured in **Siemens (S)**.
 
• The reciprocal of **resistivity** is known as **electrical conductivity (σ)**, which indicates how easily a material allows current to flow. Its **SI unit** is **Siemens per meter (S/m)**.

questions.question:
Which of the statement(s) is/are NOT true about the phenomenon of scattering of light:
(i) The amount of scattering light undergoes is independent of the size of particles of the medium through which light is passing.
(ii) The amount of scattering is directly proportional to the wavelength of light.
(iii) The colour of the sky appears blue as blue light undergoes more scattering as compared to red light.
(iv) The colour of danger signal is red as red colour undergoes least amount of scattering when passing through fog.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (i) and (ii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement (i)**: The amount of light scattering is highly dependent on the **size of the particles** in the medium. If the particles are very small compared to the wavelength of light (like **nitrogen** and **oxygen molecules** in the air), **Rayleigh scattering** occurs. If the particles are large (like **water droplets** in clouds), they scatter all wavelengths almost equally. ***Hence, statement (i) is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement (ii)**: According to **Rayleigh's Law of Scattering**, the intensity of scattered light is **inversely proportional** to the **fourth power of its wavelength** (Scattering ∝ 1/λ⁴). This means shorter wavelengths scatter much more than longer wavelengths. It is not directly proportional. ***Hence, statement (ii) is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement (iii)**: Blue light has a **shorter wavelength** compared to red light. As light from the **Sun** enters the **Earth's atmosphere**, the molecules in the air scatter the blue light more strongly in all directions. This is why the sky appears **blue** to an observer on the ground. ***Hence, statement (iii) is correct.***
 
• **Statement (iv)**: **Red light** has the **longest wavelength** in the **visible spectrum**. Due to its long wavelength, it is **scattered the least** by air molecules, **fog**, or **smoke**. This allows the red color to travel longer distances without being dispersed, making it ideal for **danger signals**. ***Hence, statement (iv) is correct.***
 
• Since statements **(i) and (ii)** are the ones that are **not true**, the correct option is **Both (i) and (ii)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rayleigh Scattering**: Formulated by **Lord Rayleigh** in **1871**, this phenomenon explains why the sky is blue. It occurs when the scattering particles have a **diameter** significantly smaller (less than **1/10th**) than the **wavelength** of the incident light.
 
• **The Visible Spectrum**: Human eyes can detect wavelengths approximately between **400 nm** (violet) and **700 nm** (red). Within this range, **violet** and **blue** have the highest frequencies and shortest wavelengths, while **red** has the lowest frequency and longest wavelength.
 
• **Tyndall Effect**: This is the scattering of a beam of light by **colloidal particles** or particles in a very fine **suspension**. It is often observed when sunlight passes through a **canopy of a dense forest** where mist or dust particles scatter the light.
 
• **Color of the Sun at Sunrise and Sunset**: During these times, sunlight must travel a **longer distance** through the atmosphere to reach our eyes. Most of the **shorter wavelengths** (blue and violet) are scattered away, leaving only the **longer wavelengths** (red and orange) to reach the observer.
 
• **Mie Scattering**: Unlike Rayleigh scattering, **Mie scattering** occurs when the particles are of a similar size to the wavelength of light. This is why **clouds** appear **white**, as large water droplets scatter all colors of light equally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Wavelength Relationship**: The relationship between wavelength and scattering explains many natural phenomena. Because red scatters the least, it is used in **tail lights** and **stop signs** for maximum **visibility** in adverse weather conditions like **rain** or **fog**.
 
• **Atmospheric Composition**: If the **Earth** had no atmosphere, there would be no scattering of light, and the **sky would appear black** even during the daytime, similar to what **astronauts** see in **outer space**.
 
• **Numerical Fact**: Because scattering is proportional to **1/λ⁴**, blue light (wavelength approx **450 nm**) is scattered about **10 times** more efficiently than red light (wavelength approx **650 nm**).

questions.question: What is the equivalent of 1 kilowatt-hour (kWh) in joules?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3.6 x 10⁶ joules**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kilowatt-hour (kWh)** is the **commercial unit** of **electrical energy**. It represents the amount of energy consumed by an electrical appliance of **1 kilowatt** power in **one hour**.
 
• To convert **1 kWh** into **Joules**, we must break down the units into their **SI base units**. **1 kilowatt** is equal to **1000 Watts**, and **1 hour** is equal to **3600 seconds** (60 minutes × 60 seconds).
 
• By definition, **1 Watt** is equal to **1 Joule per second (1 J/s)**. Therefore, the total energy in joules is calculated by multiplying power in watts by time in seconds: **1000 W × 3600 s**.
 
• Performing the calculation: **1000 × 3600 = 3,600,000 Joules**. In **scientific notation**, this value is expressed as **3.6 × 10⁶ Joules**.
 
• The statement in option 1 claims **1 kWh = 3.6 × 10³ joules**, which is incorrect as it represents only 3600 joules. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The statement in option 2 claims **1 kWh = 360 joules**, which is a significant undervaluation of the energy unit. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The statement in option 3 claims **1 kWh = 36 × 10^-6 joules**, which suggests a microscopic amount of energy. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The statement in option 4 claims **1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ joules**, which matches the derived mathematical conversion. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Difference between Power and Energy:** **Power** is the **rate** at which work is done or energy is transformed, measured in **Watts (W)**. **Energy** is the **total capacity** to do work, measured in **Joules (J)** or **kilowatt-hours (kWh)**.
 
• **Commercial Usage:** In many countries, including **India**, the electricity bill is calculated based on "units" of electricity. **1 Unit** is exactly equal to **1 kilowatt-hour (kWh)**.
 
• **SI Unit of Energy:** The **Joule** is the **Standard International (SI) unit** for energy, named after the English physicist **James Prescott Joule**. It is a derived unit equivalent to **1 Newton-meter**.
 
• **Other Units:** Energy can also be measured in **Calories** (often used in nutrition) or **electron-volts (eV)** (used in atomic physics). **1 calorie** is approximately equal to **4.184 Joules**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dimensional Formula:** The dimensional formula for **energy** (and work) is **[M¹ L² T^-2]**. This is derived from **Force × Displacement**.
 
• **Mega Joules:** Because **3.6 × 10⁶** is a large number, **1 kWh** is often referred to as **3.6 Mega Joules (MJ)**.
 
• **Historical Context:** The term **Board of Trade Unit (B.O.T.U.)** was previously used in the **United Kingdom** to describe **1 kilowatt-hour** before the metric terminology became standardized.
 
• **Practical Example:** If a **100-Watt** light bulb is left on for **10 hours**, it consumes **1 kWh** of energy (100W × 10h = 1000Wh = 1kWh).

questions.question: Which of the following is a homologous series?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Methane, Ethane, Propane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **homologous series** is a sequence of **organic compounds** that have the same **functional group** and similar **chemical properties** in which the successive members differ by a **CH2 unit**.
 
• **Methane (CH4)**, **Ethane (C2H6)**, and **Propane (C3H8)** all belong to the **Alkane** series, which follows the general formula **CnH2n+2**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• In **Methane, Methanol, and Methanoic acid**, the compounds have different functional groups (alkane, alcohol, and carboxylic acid respectively), meaning they do not belong to the same series. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• In **Ethene, Ethyne, and Ethane**, the compounds have different degrees of saturation (alkene, alkyne, and alkane), resulting in different general formulas. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• In **Methane, Ethane, and Ethene**, the first two are **alkanes** while the third is an **alkene**, so they do not form a single homologous series. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• Successive members of a homologous series like **alkanes** have a difference of **14 atomic mass units (u)** in their **molecular mass**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Homologous Series:**
 
 
• All members of a series can be represented by the same **general molecular formula**. For example, **Alkenes** follow **CnH2n** and **Alkynes** follow **CnH2n-2**.
 
• Any two adjacent members differ by a **-CH2- group** in their molecular formula.
 
• The **chemical properties** of the members are similar because they contain the same **functional group** (such as -OH for alcohols or -CHO for aldehydes).
 
• There is a gradual change in **physical properties** like **melting point**, **boiling point**, and **solubility** as the **molecular mass** increases.
 
 
 
• **Alkanes:**
 
• These are **saturated hydrocarbons** where all carbon-carbon bonds are **single bonds**.
 
• **Methane** is the simplest alkane, often called **marsh gas**, and is a primary component of **natural gas**.
 
• As the number of **carbon atoms** increases, the boiling point increases due to stronger **Van der Waals forces**.
 
 
• **Alkenes and Alkynes:**
 
• **Alkenes** contain at least one **double bond** (unsaturated) and start from **Ethene (C2H4)**.
 
• **Alkynes** contain at least one **triple bond** (unsaturated) and start from **Ethyne (C2H2)**, also known as **acetylene**.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The concept of **homology** was developed to simplify the study of millions of **organic chemistry** compounds by grouping them based on structural similarities.
 
• **Isomers** are compounds with the same **molecular formula** but different **structural arrangements**; they should not be confused with members of a homologous series.
 
• The **substitution reaction** is a characteristic chemical property of **alkanes**, while **addition reactions** are characteristic of **alkenes** and **alkynes**.
 
• In the **homologous series** of alcohols, the members would be **Methanol (CH3OH)**, **Ethanol (C2H5OH)**, **Propanol (C3H7OH)**, and so on, all differing by **-CH2-**.
</ul

questions.question: According to Rutherford's model of an atom, the radius of an atom in metre is about:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10⁻¹⁰**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Rutherford model** of the atom, the **radius of an atom** is approximately **10⁻¹⁰ metres**. This value is also commonly referred to as **1 Angstrom (Å)** in atomic physics.
 
• In contrast, the **radius of the nucleus** is much smaller, estimated to be about **10⁻¹⁵ metres**, which is equivalent to **1 femtometre** or **1 Fermi**.
 
• This implies that the **atom** is about **10⁵ (100,000) times larger** than its **nucleus**. If an atom were expanded to the size of a large football stadium, the nucleus would be about the size of a small marble placed at the center.
 
• **Ernest Rutherford** derived these dimensions based on his famous **Alpha-particle scattering experiment** conducted in **1911**, where he observed how **alpha particles** interacted with a **thin gold foil**.
 
• The model concluded that since most alpha particles passed through the foil undeflected, the vast majority of an **atom's volume** is **empty space**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the radius being 10⁻¹⁰ metres is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rutherford’s Gold Foil Experiment:**
 
 
• In this experiment, high-energy **alpha particles** (Helium nuclei) were directed at a **thin gold foil** of about **100 nm** thickness.
 
• Observations showed that about **99%** of the particles passed straight through, while a very small fraction was deflected by **large angles**, and about **1 in 12,000** particles rebounded completely (180 degrees).
 
• This led to the discovery of the **Atomic Nucleus**, proving that the positive charge and most of the **mass of the atom** are concentrated in a tiny central region.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Rutherford's Atomic Model:**
 
 
• The **nucleus** is positively charged and contains nearly all the **mass** of the atom.
 
• The **electrons** revolve around the nucleus in well-defined **circular orbits**, much like planets revolving around the Sun. This is why it is often called the **Planetary Model**.
 
• The **electrostatic force of attraction** between the nucleus and the electrons holds the atom together.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of the Model:**
 
 
• The primary drawback was its inability to explain **atomic stability**. According to **Maxwell’s electromagnetic theory**, an accelerating charged particle (like an orbiting electron) should radiate energy.
 
• If an electron continuously lost energy, its **orbital radius** would decrease, eventually causing it to spiral into the nucleus, making the atom unstable. This was later addressed by **Niels Bohr** in **1913**.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Legacy of Ernest Rutherford:**
 
 
• **Ernest Rutherford** is hailed as the **Father of Nuclear Physics**.
 
• He was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Chemistry** in **1908** for his investigations into the disintegration of elements and the chemistry of radioactive substances.
 
• He also successfully performed the first **artificial transmutation** of an element in **1919**, converting nitrogen into oxygen by bombarding it with alpha particles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison of Scales:** While the atom is **10⁻¹⁰ m**, the **Proton** has a radius of approximately **0.84 to 0.87 femtometres**.
 
• **Measurement Units:** 1 **Angstrom** (Å) = **10⁻¹⁰ metres** = **0.1 nanometres**. This scale is fundamental for measuring **bond lengths** and **atomic sizes** in chemistry.
 
• **Density of the Nucleus:** Because almost all mass is in the tiny nucleus, the **density of the nucleus** is extremely high, approximately **2.3 x 10¹⁷ kg/m³**.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of cell division in multicellular organisms?

options.text: Formation of vacuoles and maintenance of turgidity
Transport of substances through the cell membrane
Absorption of nutrients and release of wastes
Growth, repair, and replacement of damaged or old cells

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Growth, repair, and replacement of damaged or old cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cell division** is a fundamental biological process by which a **parent cell** divides into two or more **daughter cells**, primarily serving the needs of **growth** and **maintenance** in **multicellular organisms**.
 
• **Growth**: Every multicellular organism starts its life as a single cell called a **zygote**. Through successive rounds of **mitotic cell division**, the number of cells increases, leading to the development of **tissues**, **organs**, and the overall body structure.
 
• **Repair**: When an organism suffers an injury, such as a cut on the skin or a broken bone, **cell division** is activated at the site of the damage to produce new cells that fill the wound and restore the structural integrity of the **tissue**.
 
• **Replacement**: Cells in a multicellular body have a finite lifespan and are constantly being worn out. For example, **Red Blood Cells (RBCs)** in humans have a lifespan of approximately **120 days**, and **skin cells** are shed regularly; hence, **cell division** is essential to replace these **dead or damaged cells** to keep the organism healthy.
 
• **Genetic Continuity**: It ensures that the **genetic information (DNA)** is accurately passed from one generation of cells to the next, maintaining the **biological blueprint** of the organism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Cell Division**:
 
 
• **Mitosis**: Also known as **equational division**, it occurs in **somatic cells** (body cells). It results in two daughter cells that are genetically identical to the parent cell, each containing a **diploid (2n)** number of **chromosomes**.
 
• **Meiosis**: Known as **reduction division**, it occurs in **germ cells** to produce **gametes** (sperm and eggs). It reduces the chromosome number by half to **haploid (n)**, ensuring that the **diploid** number is restored upon **fertilization**.
 
 
 
• **The Cell Cycle**: The process of division is part of a larger cycle comprising **Interphase** (the growth and **DNA replication** phase) and the **M-phase** (the actual division phase). The **S-phase** within Interphase is critical as it is the period when **DNA synthesis** occurs.
 
• **Regulation of Cell Division**: In healthy organisms, cell division is strictly regulated by **proteins** and **checkpoints**. If this regulation fails, cells may divide uncontrollably, which is the primary cause of **cancer** and **tumor formation**.
 
• **Analysis of Other Options**:
 
 
• **Vacuoles and Turgidity**: This is a function of the **cell organelle** (specifically in plants), not the purpose of division. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Transport of substances**: This is managed by the **cell membrane** through **osmosis**, **diffusion**, and **active transport**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Absorption and Waste Release**: These are **metabolic** and **excretory** functions performed by the cell during its **interphase** life. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chromosomes**: During division, **chromatin** condenses into visible **chromosomes**. Humans have **23 pairs** (total **46**) of chromosomes.
 
• **Cytokinesis**: This is the physical process of **cytoplasmic division** that follows **karyokinesis** (nuclear division) to finally split one cell into two.
 
• **Regeneration**: Some organisms, like **Planaria** or **Starfish**, use specialized **cell division** to regrow entire lost body parts, showing an extreme form of the **repair** function.
</ul
